newsitem.title: USA: Kansas unemployment rate rises to 4.0 pct in June.
newsitem.headline: Kansas unemployment rate rises to 4.0 pct in June.

text.p: Kansas' unemployment rate rose to 4 percent in June from 3.8 percent in May, but still remained far below the 4.8 percent recorded a year ago, the state human resources department reported Monday.
Employment in June rose to more then 1.35 million, setting a new record, reflecting an increase of 51,000 over June 1996, department Secretary Wayne Franklin said.
June is the state's traditional peak employment month and seasonal workers pushed employment and unemployment numbers higher, Franklin said.
"The increases over the month reflect Kansas' seasonal trend," Franklin said. "Thousands of students and other seasonal workers join the labor force at this time of year."
Construction and retail trade sectors reported the biggest increases in jobs, with the wheat harvest spurring wholesale trade jobs at elevators, Franklin said.
The government sector reported the only employment losses for the month, due to seasonal furloughs at state and local schools.
